scenes.tts: A dorsal lip moved to a new place can give a second body axis. But whose cells built it?
scenes.visual: Title card: Whose Cells Built It? A gastrula with a second axis rising on its flank.
scenes.narration: A dorsal lip moved to a new place can give a second body axis. But whose cells built it?

scenes.tts: Grafts within one species had given extra axial structures. But donor and host cells look alike.
scenes.visual: Two embryos of one species, same colour; a moved dorsal lip gives extra axial structures. Zoom: donor and host cells identical.
scenes.narration: Grafts within one species had given extra axial structures. But donor and host cells look alike.

scenes.tts: So, two readings for the new neural tube. Self-differentiation: the graft's cells develop by their own origin, and make the tube themselves.
scenes.visual: Hypothesis card 1: self-differentiation. The second neural tube is donor cells. Small note: in its own embryo, the dorsal lip mainly makes notochord and dorsal mesoderm.
scenes.narration: So, two readings for the new neural tube. Self-differentiation: the graft's cells develop by their own origin, and make the tube themselves.

scenes.tts: Or induction: the graft changes the fate of its neighbours, and host cells build the new tube.
scenes.visual: Hypothesis card 2: induction. The second neural tube is host cells.
scenes.narration: Or induction: the graft changes the fate of its neighbours, and host cells build the new tube.

scenes.tts: The solution was colour. Hilde Mangold did the test in Hans Spemann's laboratory, for her doctoral thesis.
scenes.visual: Credit: Hilde Mangold, doctoral student, Spemann's laboratory, Freiburg.
scenes.narration: The solution was colour. Hilde Mangold did the test in Hans Spemann's laboratory, for her doctoral thesis.

scenes.tts: She used two newt species. Cells of one carry little pigment. Cells of the other carry pigment granules.
scenes.visual: A pale embryo, labelled Triton cristatus: little pigment. A dark embryo, labelled Triton taeniatus: pigment granules.
scenes.narration: She used two newt species. Cells of one carry little pigment. Cells of the other carry pigment granules.

scenes.tts: The granules stay visible in sections, so colour shows which embryo a cell came from.
scenes.visual: A thin section with dark granules in each host cell. Label: lineage marker. Pale cell, donor; pigmented cell, host.
scenes.narration: The granules stay visible in sections, so colour shows which embryo a cell came from.

scenes.tts: In nineteen twenty-one and nineteen twenty-two, she cut a piece of dorsal lip from a pale gastrula.
scenes.caption: In 1921 and 1922, she cut a piece of dorsal lip from a pale gastrula.
scenes.visual: A small piece is cut from the dorsal lip of the pale gastrula. Dates on screen: 1921 and 1922.
scenes.narration: In 1921 and 1922, she cut a piece of dorsal lip from a pale gastrula.

scenes.tts: She placed it in the belly of a pigmented gastrula, in tissue that would normally become skin.
scenes.visual: Simplified graft: the pale piece is pushed into the belly of the dark gastrula. Labels: future belly skin; host stages in the series varied.
scenes.narration: She placed it in the belly of a pigmented gastrula, in tissue that would normally become skin.

scenes.tts: Most embryos died. In the survivors, a second neural plate rose, folded, and closed into a second neural tube.
scenes.visual: Most operated embryos fade out. On a survivor, a second neural plate rises on the flank, folds and closes.
scenes.narration: Most embryos died. In the survivors, a second neural plate rose, folded, and closed into a second neural tube.

scenes.tts: Predict. If the graft simply grew, what colour is the new tube? If it changed its neighbours?
scenes.visual: Prediction table, rows 1 and 2: self-differentiation, colour?; induction, colour?
scenes.narration: Predict. If the graft simply grew, what colour is the new tube? If it changed its neighbours?

scenes.tts: If the graft grew, the tube should be pale. If it changed its neighbours, the tube should be pigmented.
scenes.visual: Table fills in: self-differentiation, nearly all pale; induction, nearly all pigmented. Row 3: both, a mix; host cells still show induction.
scenes.narration: If the graft grew, the tube should be pale. If it changed its neighbours, the tube should be pigmented.

scenes.tts: In one embryo, most of the second tube was pigmented, with a narrow pale strip along its floor.
scenes.visual: A cross-section drawn in the style of Mangold's figures: dark host cells fill most of the second tube; a narrow pale strip on its floor.
scenes.narration: In one embryo, most of the second tube was pigmented, with a narrow pale strip along its floor.

scenes.tts: In another, the whole tube was host tissue. The pale graft lay beneath it, as a notochord and nearby mesoderm.
scenes.visual: Second section: tube entirely dark host cells; below it a pale rod labelled second notochord, with pale nearby mesoderm.
scenes.narration: In another, the whole tube was host tissue. The pale graft lay beneath it, as a notochord and nearby mesoderm.

scenes.tts: Host ectoderm that would have made skin had made a neural tube. For the tube, induction explained it.
scenes.visual: Hypothesis card 2 lights up for the neural tube. A new card appears beside it: the graft's own cells became notochord (self-differentiation). Label: both happened.
scenes.narration: Host ectoderm that would have made skin had made a neural tube. For the tube, induction explained it.

scenes.tts: Induction is a change in the fate of one tissue, caused by a signal from another.
scenes.visual: Definition card: induction.
scenes.narration: Induction is a change in the fate of one tissue, caused by a signal from another.

scenes.tts: The graft did three things. Its own cells became notochord.
scenes.visual: Three-role list builds. Role 1: own cells become notochord (pale).
scenes.narration: The graft did three things. Its own cells became notochord.

scenes.tts: It recruited host mesoderm into somites, blocks beside the tube that form vertebrae and muscle.
scenes.visual: Role 2: recruits host mesoderm; blocks labelled somites appear beside the tube, with vertebra and muscle icons.
scenes.narration: It recruited host mesoderm into somites, blocks beside the tube that form vertebrae and muscle.

scenes.tts: And it induced host ectoderm to become a neural tube. Hence the name, organizer.
scenes.visual: Role 3: induces host ectoderm. Label over the whole axis: organizer.
scenes.narration: And it induced host ectoderm to become a neural tube. Hence the name, organizer.

scenes.tts: The second axis formed at the graft, not along the host's own back.
scenes.visual: Top view: host's own axis along the back; the second axis on the flank, where the graft sat.
scenes.narration: The second axis formed at the graft, not along the host's own back.

scenes.tts: The pattern followed the source. So the organizer decides where neural tissue forms.
scenes.visual: Card: move the source, the pattern follows: it sets where.
scenes.narration: The pattern followed the source. So the organizer decides where neural tissue forms.

scenes.tts: It does not yet say how: by a go signal, or by releasing a brake.
scenes.visual: Card adds: how? a go signal, or a released brake. Open question.
scenes.narration: It does not yet say how: by a go signal, or by releasing a brake.

scenes.tts: The responder must also be able to answer. That ability is competence.
scenes.visual: Two parties on screen: inducer sends, responder answers. Label on responder: competence.
scenes.narration: The responder must also be able to answer. That ability is competence.

scenes.tts: Wrap older and older ectoderm around early organizer. The response falls, and largely stops by the end of gastrulation.
scenes.visual: Bar chart, labelled hypothetical numbers: early, mid, late gastrula, early neurula ectoderm; bars 90, 70, 15, 0 percent neural.
scenes.narration: Wrap older and older ectoderm around early organizer. The response falls, and largely stops by the end of gastrulation.

scenes.tts: The control: late organizer with young ectoderm. If that still works, the loss is in the responder.
scenes.visual: Extra bar: late organizer with early-gastrula ectoderm, 85 percent, hypothetical. Label: the loss is in the responder.
scenes.narration: The control: late organizer with young ectoderm. If that still works, the loss is in the responder.

scenes.tts: So host cells built the second neural tube, at the graft, while they could still answer.
scenes.visual: Closing card: host cells built the tube, at the graft, while competent.
scenes.narration: So host cells built the second neural tube, at the graft, while they could still answer.
